name: Coca
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Only minimal/comparative colonial-wordlist studies exist (Dávila Garibi 1935, 1942; Torres Nila & Yáñez Rosales 2018); extinct, no phonological description.

sources.note: Nothing. Reproduces a comparative vocabulary table from Dávila Garibi and two toponyms from the Relación Geográfica; cites only the three works above. Gave the academia.edu URL for the 2018 chapter.

sources.citation: Dávila Garibi, J. Ignacio. 1935. Recopilación de datos acerca del idioma coca y de su posible influencia en el lenguaje folklórico de Jalisco. Investigaciones Lingüísticas (México) III: 248–302.
sources.note: Nothing. Ethnohistorical compilation (sources, geography, colonial language policy, etymologies, Jalisco regionalisms) plus a short comparative wordlist (p. 300, Spanish/Coca/Caxcan/Aztec/Tarascan/Cora) and a 19th-c. vocabulary from Rodríguez Nixen (pp. 283–285). No accent marks on Coca forms, no pronunciation or accent remarks; the only 'acento' on p. 251 refers to the Spanish of Jalisco. The author states (p. 249) that no dictionaries, grammars or Coca literature exist and (p. 266) that Coca is a dead language with no known literature.

sources.citation: Yáñez Rosales, Rosa H. [ca. 2004]. Los caminos de la diversidad lingüística: el Occidente de México, del siglo XVI al siglo XXI. In José Luis Iturrioz Leza et al., Lenguas y literaturas indígenas de Jalisco (Las culturas populares de Jalisco, 4), 281–302. Guadalajara: Secretaría de Cultura, Gobierno del Estado de Jalisco. [chapter signed Guadalajara, Agosto de 2003; publisher PDF carries no imprint page, volume year not verified]
sources.note: Read pp. 281-302 in full (text, a full-text search for stress/accent tono/tonal/acento/prosod/fonol/vocal/sílaba: no hits in the chapter). Coca appears only as an extinct language of the Sayula-Chapala basins, assigned to the Taracahitan branch 'por las pocas referencias que conocemos', known from 'sólo una breve lista de palabras'; no forms are analysed, no orthography, stress or tone remarks. Confirms that no phonological statement on Coca exists in the accessible modern literature.

tone.quote: Dicho grupo era el coca, del cual tenemos sólo una breve lista de palabras rescatadas en el siglo XVI, en las Relaciones Geográficas (Acuña, 1988) y otra lista rescatada por Ignacio Dávila Garibi (1935, 1943), en Cocula, en el siglo XX.
tone.locator: p. 282, first paragraph; preceded on p. 281 by 'por las pocas referencias que conocemos de la misma, es una lengua que pertenece a la rama taracahita'
tone.translation: That group was the Coca, of which we have only a short list of words recovered in the sixteenth century, in the Relaciones Geográficas (Acuña 1988), and another list recovered by Ignacio Dávila Garibi (1935, 1943) in Cocula in the twentieth century.
tone.says: Read pp. 281-302 in full (text, a full-text search for stress/accent tono/tonal/acento/prosod/fonol/vocal/sílaba: no hits in the chapter). Coca appears only as an extinct language of the Sayula-Chapala basins, assigned to the Taracahitan branch 'por las pocas referencias que conocemos', known from 'sólo una breve lista de palabras'; no forms are analysed, no orthography, stress or tone remarks. Confirms that no phonological statement on Coca exists in the accessible modern literature.
